name: Titanic
blurb: White Star liner, sank in the North Atlantic on 15 April 1912 · her radio operators sent both the old CQD distress call and the brand-new SOS, making her one of the first ships to use it at sea

name: United States Declaration of Independence
blurb: Adopted by the Second Continental Congress, 4 July 1776 · most of the signatures we see today weren't added until 2 August — only Hancock and the secretary signed on the day itself
attribution: William Stone (1823 facsimile), after the Second Continental Congress
source: Wikimedia Commons: United States Declaration of Independence.jpg
image_author: original: Second Continental Congress; reproduction: William Stone

name: United States Constitution
blurb: Signed at the Philadelphia Convention, 17 September 1787 · at roughly 4,400 words, it's the shortest written constitution of any major world power still in force
source: Wikimedia Commons: Constitution of the United States - DPLA - 9ca804144bd5965e992ae3528bc3c6a3 (page 1).jpg

name: Berlin Wall
blurb: Divided East and West Berlin from 13 August 1961 to 9 November 1989 · West Berliners covered their side in graffiti for decades — the East German side stayed a blank, heavily guarded 'death strip'
source: Wikimedia Commons: Berlin Wall Potsdamer Platz November 1975 looking east crop.jpg

name: Empire State Building
blurb: Completed in 1931 in just 410 days · its planned mooring mast for airships was abandoned after one attempt nearly blew a delivery blimp off its tether
source: Wikimedia Commons: Empire State Building (aerial view).jpg

name: Space Shuttle
blurb: NASA's reusable orbiter fleet, first flew in 1981 · Discovery alone flew 39 missions — more spaceflights than any other single spacecraft in history

name: World Trade Center
blurb: Twin towers completed 1972–1973 · the north tower briefly held the world's-tallest-building title before Chicago's Sears Tower overtook it in 1973
source: Wikimedia Commons: World Trade Center, New York City - aerial view (March 2001).jpg

name: White House
blurb: Home to every US president since John Adams in 1800 · British troops burned it in August 1814 — a sudden thunderstorm that same night likely saved its stone walls from total collapse

name: Kaaba
blurb: Cube-shaped shrine at the centre of Mecca's Grand Mosque, rebuilt in its current form in 1629–1630 · the black silk kiswah draping it is taken down and rewoven fresh every single year for Hajj

name: Louvre
blurb: Former royal palace turned museum, opened to the public in 1793 · its glass pyramid entrance, added in 1989, was so controversial at first that critics compared it to a dagger through the historic courtyard
source: Wikimedia Commons: Cour Napoléon at night - Louvre.jpg

name: Shroud of Turin
blurb: Linen cloth bearing a faint body image, first documented in the 1350s · radiocarbon dating in 1988 placed its fabric in the medieval period, though disputes over the test continue

name: Saturn V
blurb: NASA's Moon rocket, first launched in 1967 · across all 13 flights — Apollo 4 through 17 plus the Skylab launch — it never suffered a single failure

name: Domesday Book
blurb: William the Conqueror's survey of England, completed in 1086 · its findings were so exhaustive and final that Anglo-Saxons nicknamed it 'Domesday' after the Last Judgement — nothing in it could be appealed

name: Little Boy
blurb: Uranium gun-type bomb dropped on Hiroshima, 6 August 1945 · unlike its plutonium cousin tested at Trinity that July, Little Boy's design was never test-fired before that first live drop
attribution: US Atomic Energy Commission (now US Department of Energy)
image_author: US Atomic Energy Commission (now US Department of Energy)

name: HMS Victory
blurb: Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar, launched in 1765 · she's still a commissioned Royal Navy warship today, the oldest in the world still on the active list

name: Ajanta Caves
blurb: Buddhist rock-cut cave complex, carved between the 2nd century BC and 6th century AD · abandoned for over a thousand years, it was only rediscovered in 1819 when a British officer chasing a tiger stumbled on one entrance

name: Sydney Opera House
blurb: Jørn Utzon's harbour-side design, opened in 1973 · the sail-like shells took over a decade longer to engineer than planned, since no one had worked out how to actually build the curved roof shapes he'd sketched

name: Voyager Golden Record
blurb: Gold-plated phonograph disc launched aboard both Voyager probes in 1977 · it carries a sample of uranium-238 etched into its cover, so any finder could calculate exactly how long it had been travelling
source: Wikimedia Commons: The Sounds of Earth Record Cover - GPN-2000-001978.jpg

name: Palace of Westminster
blurb: Seat of the UK Parliament, rebuilt after an 1834 fire destroyed almost the whole medieval palace · only Westminster Hall, with its 14th-century hammerbeam roof, survived largely intact
source: Wikimedia Commons: Houses of Parliament in 2022 (cropped).jpg
image_author: Terry Ott from Washington, DC Metro Area, United States of America

name: Sistine Chapel
blurb: Pope Sixtus IV's private chapel, completed in 1483 · its side walls were frescoed by an earlier generation of masters — Botticelli and Perugino among them — years before Michelangelo ever touched the ceiling
